AdmissionRule.description: Per-project admission limits (#7), plus the runtime-env governance knobs (#52) PR #74 hardcoded into the validator — carried here so they are API-editable. All fields optional; a zero value means unrestricted / the governed default. Keyed by project (or `"*"` for every project) in `PolicyView.admission`.

allow_conda.description: Permit the runtime_env conda field (an environment file whose channels the control plane cannot audit); false = denied (#53).

allow_image_uri.description: Permit the runtime_env image_uri field (an arbitrary per-worker container image, bypassing allowed_images); false = denied (#53).

allow_py_executable.description: Permit the runtime_env py_executable field (an interpreter binary the platform cannot attest); false = denied (#53).

allow_unpinned_packages.description: Permit pip entries not pinned to an exact version; false = name==version required (#53).

allowed_images.description: Container images a cluster/job in the project may use; empty = any image.

allowed_index_hosts.description: Hosts trusted as package indexes: pip_install_options may redirect --index-url/--extra-index-url/--find-links only to one of these; empty = no index redirection at all (#53).

allowed_remote_hosts.description: Hosts remote working_dir/py_modules URIs may point at (with allowed_remote_schemes); empty = local uploads only (#53).

allowed_remote_schemes.description: URI schemes remote working_dir/py_modules may use (with allowed_remote_hosts); empty = local uploads only (#53).

catalog_only.description: Require a cluster/job's image to be an image catalog entry (#10) open to the project; false = `allowed_images` alone decides.

max_document_bytes.description: Cap on the raw runtime_env_yaml document size; 0 = the platform default (64 KiB) (#53).

max_setup_timeout_seconds.description: Cap on runtime_env config.setup_timeout_seconds; 0 = the platform default (600) (#53).

max_workers.description: Maximum total worker replicas across all worker groups; 0 = unlimited.

package_denylist.description: PyPI-normalized package names (PEP 503) that must never install, pinned or not (#53).

require_scanned_environments.description: Require every environment a spec references to carry a clean recorded scan verdict (#58): a reference to an environment whose `scan` is absent, pending or failed is refused (400); false = any published environment is referenceable.

AllocationSpec.description:
A project's allocation within a pool (translates to a Kueue LocalQueue).

`nominal` / `borrowing_limit` / `lending_limit` are reserved for a future
per-project ClusterQueue layout (ADR-0010): in the v0 layout all
allocations in a pool share one ClusterQueue, so these are recorded as
LocalQueue annotations rather than enforced quotas.

ApiTokenView.description: The public projection of an API token — no hash, no plaintext.

AssignmentView.description: One assignment as the wire sees it.

created_at.description: Unix seconds when the assignment was first written.

principal.description:
The principal the assignment applies to: a token `sub` (opaque
Keycloak UUID) or a `preferred_username` — evaluation matches BOTH, so
human-friendly username grants take effect (#88).

AuditDecision.description:
Whether Bifrost allowed or refused the thing the event describes.
Serialized snake_case (`allow` / `deny`).

AuditEvent.description:
One audit-trail row (api-v1.md §5.9). Fields not applicable to the
emitting site are `None` (serialized `null`); `granted_roles` is empty.

Decision policy (the audit subsystem): `deny` rows are emitted at
the point of refusal (authn failures, authz denials, quota denials);
gateway per-request rows are always `allow` — a request Bifrost refuses
never reaches the gateway, so its `deny` row comes from the refuser.

cluster.description: Cluster id the event concerns; `null` when not cluster-scoped.

granted_roles.description: Roles the caller held (snake_case); authz denials only, else `[]`.

method.description: HTTP method, for gateway and authn/ext_authz rows.

oneOf.description: The permission an authz denial was checked against.

status.description: HTTP status of the outcome, when one is known.

subject.description: Authenticated subject; `null` for authn failures (no identity yet).

AuditListResponse.description:
Response of `GET /api/v1/audit`. This endpoint is the ONE list route
that wraps its items in an envelope — the cursor has to live somewhere
(api-v1.md §5.9).

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next (older) page; `null` at the end.

AuditRequired.description:
The (verb, target) permission an authorization decision was checked
against — mirrors the auth subsystem's permission/target vocabulary as lowercase
strings (`"write"`, `"cluster"`) so core stays free of auth types.
Present only on authz denials.

events_checked.description:
Rows that verified before the replay stopped (the whole window on
success; the rows before the broken one on failure).

first_broken_seq.description:
Seq of the first row whose stored `chain_hash` doesn't match the
replay; `null` when the window verifies clean.

ok.description: True when every row in the window matched the replayed chain.

BudgetStatus.description:
A configured project's time-windowed budget status (#77): the cap, what
has been consumed over the trailing window (ending at the report's `to`),
and what remains. Distinct from `UsageGroup` — this reflects the
`[budgets]` policy, not the raw sample roll-up.

consumed.description: resource → resource-hours consumed over the trailing window.

exhausted.description:
True once consumption has reached or passed the cap on any capped
resource — a create for this project would be 409'd.

limit.description: resource → resource-hours allowed over the window.

remaining.description:
resource → resource-hours remaining (`limit − consumed`, floored at 0)
for each capped resource.

additionalProperties.description:
resource → resource-hours allowed over the window (`cpu` = core-hours,
`memory` = GiB-hours, `nvidia.com/gpu` = GPU-hours).

BudgetView.description: A configured budget as reported by the settings API.

window_secs.description: Trailing window length in seconds (e.g. 604800 = 7 days).

ClusterEvent.description:
One normalized Kubernetes Event about a cluster object (api-v1.md §5.8).
Fields are `Option` because the two Event schemas (core/v1 and
events.k8s.io/v1) name them differently and any of them may be absent.

count.description:
How many times this event has fired (K8s collapses repeats). Defaults
to 1 when the source records no count.

first_seen.description: First occurrence (RFC3339); `None` when the source omits it.

last_seen.description: Most recent occurrence (RFC3339); the field the list is sorted by.

object.description: The object the event is about, as `Kind/name` (e.g. `Pod/foo-head-abc`).

ClusterEvents.description:
Kubernetes Events for one cluster's objects (api-v1.md §5.8), newest first
and capped — the body of `GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/events`.

events.description: Normalized events, most-recent-first, capped (see the endpoint's cap).

ClusterLogs.description:
A tail-capped pod log view for one cluster (api-v1.md §5.6, non-streaming
first cut) — the body of `GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/logs`. WS streaming is
the eventual design (Milestone C); this GET-tail form removes the
pending-backend stub now.

lines.description: The most recent log lines (up to `tail`), oldest first.

pod.description:
The pod these `lines` are from (the requested pod, or the head pod when
none was requested). Empty only when the cluster has no pods yet.

pods.description:
Names of the cluster's pods the caller may tail (head first), so the UI
can offer a pod selector.

tail.description: The tail line count that was requested.

truncated.description: `true` when the tail was filled (there may be older lines beyond it).

ClusterMetrics.description:
Normalized cluster resource-usage summary (the body of
`GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/metrics`), distilled from the Ray dashboard's
autoscaler / load-metrics report. Every stat is `Option` because a cluster
may not report GPUs, and an older/mismatched Ray may omit a field — the UI
renders a tile only for the stats present.

active_nodes.description: Active Ray nodes the autoscaler reports; `None` when unavailable.

oneOf.description: CPU cores used vs total across the Ray cluster.

failed_nodes.description: Nodes the autoscaler marked failed; `None` when unavailable.

oneOf.description: Object-store memory bytes used vs total.

ClusterNodes.description:
Head + per-worker-group node breakdown for one cluster (api-v1.md §5.3),
the body of `GET /api/v1/clusters/{id}/nodes`.

oneOf.description: The head node; `None` if KubeRay has not created the head pod yet.

worker_groups.description: One entry per worker group, in the RayCluster spec's order.

ClusterSpec.description:
Declarative spec for a managed cluster.

Historically Ray-only (fields mirror a RayCluster CR so the KubeRay
provisioner stays a thin translation). Multi-engine adds [`Self::engine`];
the head/scheduler + worker-group shape is generic to both engines. For
`engine = dask`, `ray_version` is unused (Dask's version is carried by
[`Self::image`]); it stays a required field only for back-compat with
stored Ray specs and existing clients.

engine.description:
Which compute engine backs this cluster. `#[serde(default)]` = Ray, so
every pre-multi-engine spec and every Ray client keeps working
untouched.

environment.description: Environment catalog name (#52) whose image, packages and env vars this cluster runs with; `null` = none. Accepted and stored; resolution arrives with the catalog issue.

idle_timeout_secs.description:
**Inactivity reap window** in seconds (#100): the cluster is reaped once
it has been *idle* — no job activity — for this long, so a busy cluster
survives past it while a genuinely unused one is released. Distinct from
[`Self::ttl_seconds`], which still caps absolute age independently:
whichever fires first reaps the cluster.

Activity is derived from the persisted job history (a running/recent
gateway job keeps the cluster alive). **Limitation:** interactive Ray
Client / Dask sessions submit no gateway jobs, so their activity is
invisible to this signal — an interactive-only cluster looks idle from
creation. For such sessions rely on [`Self::ttl_seconds`] or leave this
unset. See `reconcile.rs` module docs.

`#[serde(default)]` so specs persisted before this field — and any
client that omits it — keep the prior max-age-only behavior.

owner.description:
The authenticated owner of this cluster (tier-2 owned session
clusters): the human identity that requested it — a
`preferred_username` when the OIDC token carries one, else the `sub`.
Set control-plane-side from the request identity (never trusted from
the client body); `None` for clusters created without an owner (e.g.
admin/service paths). When set it is stamped as the
`bifrost.dev/owner` label on the RayCluster and its pods, and drives
the per-owner Ray-client (`:10001`) ingress NetworkPolicy so only the
owner's notebook pod can reach the cluster. `#[serde(default)]` keeps
specs persisted before this field deserializable (they parse as
`None`).

profile.description: Profile catalog name (#7) whose shape fills zero-valued fields of this spec; conflicting non-empty fields are refused (400). `null` = none.

storage.description: Storage catalog entries (#12) delivered to the cluster's pods; the API never carries the secrets themselves.

ttl_seconds.description:
**Absolute max-age cap** in seconds: the cluster is reaped this long
after creation regardless of activity. `None` disables the max-age
reaper. (Despite the historical name, this is a wall-clock age cap, not
an inactivity window — see [`Self::idle_timeout_secs`] for that.)

ClusterState.description: Lifecycle states of a managed cluster (PLAN.md §3.1).

ClusterView.description:
A cluster as the control plane sees it: desired spec metadata plus the
last observed state (reconstructed from the provisioner, ADR-0006).

condition.description:
Drift/health alarm raised by the reconcile engine (ADR-0004, #41/#47):
"spec_drift" (out-of-band edit) or "degraded". `None` when converging
normally. Distinct from `observed_state`.

engine.description:
Which engine backs this cluster: "ray" | "dask" (multi-engine). Lets
GET /clusters surface a Ray and a Dask cluster side by side.

est_min_hourly.description: Estimated $/hr at min size, if a price sheet is configured.

gateway_url.description: Gateway address of the cluster's Ray dashboard/Jobs API while it is registered; `null` otherwise.

generation.description: Bumps when the spec changes; drives the reconcile idempotency key.

observed_state.description: Observed lifecycle state, if the cluster has been reconciled.

owner.description: Identity that created the cluster (server-stamped); `null` when unattributed.

queue.description: Kueue LocalQueue the cluster was admitted through; `null` when Kueue is not in use.

CreateCluster.description: Request body for creating/updating a managed cluster.

id.description: Stable cluster id (also the gateway routing key / RayCluster name).

CreatePool.description: Request body for creating a pool.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days; capped at the server maximum (90).

CreateTokenResponse.description:
`POST /api/v1/auth/tokens` success body. The plaintext `token` is
returned ONLY here — store it now; it cannot be recovered.

password.description:
Minimum 8 characters; bcrypt-hashed at rest, never stored or
returned in plaintext.

DeployService.description: Request body to deploy or update a service.

Engine.description:
The compute engine a cluster is provisioned on (multi-engine spike). The
control plane is engine-neutral above the provisioner seam; this
discriminator is what the reconciler and the provisioner router dispatch
on. `Ray` is the default so specs persisted before multi-engine — and any
client that omits the field — still deserialize as Ray clusters, exactly
as before.

EnvironmentScan.description: The recorded vulnerability-scan verdict for an environment (#52): an administrator records the outcome of the offline scan workflow (trivy/grype on the base image, pip-audit on the package list) here; the control plane does not scan itself.

EnvironmentSpec.description: A named, governed compute environment in the environment catalog (#52): the base image, pinned packages and env vars a job or cluster gets when its spec names this environment (`RayJobSpec.environment`, `ClusterSpec.environment`). Environments compile to a governed runtime_env (#53); `runtime_env_yaml` is the documented escape hatch. Inert in #52: references are accepted and stored, resolution arrives with the catalog issue.

base_image.description: Container image the environment builds on; admission image allowlists apply to it as to any spec image.

env_vars.description: Environment variables every workload using this environment runs with; empty = none.

name.description: Catalog name a spec refers to (an RFC 1123 label, so it can ride Kubernetes object names).

packages.description: Pip requirements, each pinned to an exact version (`name[extras]==version`) — the same pin rule the runtime_env governance validator (#53) enforces. Empty = the base image alone.

projects.description: Projects that may use this environment; empty = every project.

published_at.description: When the environment was published; `null` while in draft.

published_by.description: The identity that published the environment; `null` while in draft.

runtime_env_yaml.description: Escape hatch: an extra Ray runtime_env YAML document merged in at resolution time, governed by the same validator (#53) a job's own runtime_env_yaml passes. Empty = none.

scan.description: The scan verdict recorded for this environment; `null` = never scanned. Absent or `null` in a request means unscanned; the server always writes the field (`null` when there is no verdict).

status.description: Lifecycle state: a draft is editable and not yet selectable, published is selectable by specs, deprecated stays resolvable for existing references but should not be picked for new work. Absent = draft.

FlavorSpec.description:
A hardware flavor within a pool: node selection plus per-resource
nominal quota (K8s quantity strings, e.g. "4", "512Gi").

resources.description: Resource key → nominal quota quantity string.

GpuSharing.description:
How a pool's GPUs may be shared between workloads (#58).

NVIDIA GPU time-slicing (and fractional `nvidia.com/gpu` requests via the
device plugin) shares one GPU's SMs across processes with no hardware
isolation — acceptable within one tenant, never across tenants. MIG is
hardware partitioning and whole-GPU allocation needs no sharing at all,
so both are isolation-safe. The tenant-isolation rule itself is enforced
by the policy package's GPU admission logic at admission time; this field is the per-pool
knob it evaluates.

projects.description:
The projects the caller holds scoped grants in, from group-derived
project roles and stored assignments alike, sorted by name.

Distinct from `roles`, which lists the caller's *global* roles: a global
operator may act in every project and this list can name none, so a
client that finds it empty should read `roles` before concluding the
caller may do nothing.

ImageConfig.description: The image config blob as the OCI image spec defines it: what a container from this image starts with.

env.description: Environment variables, split at the first `=`.

ImageEntry.description: An approved container image (#7/#10): a reference an administrator vetted, with its engine and Ray version spelled out instead of guessed from the tag. Specs still carry `image` as a string; when a project's admission rule is `catalog_only` that string must be an entry's `ref` (or `repo@digest` when pinned), and an entry's `ray_version` fills a spec that leaves it empty. An environment's `base_image` is admitted through the same rule.

digest.description: Manifest digest `ref` is pinned to (`sha256:…`); empty = unpinned, the tag is followed.

engine.description: Engine the image carries; absent = ray.

name.description: Catalog name clients show and pick.

projects.description: Projects that may use this image; empty = every project.

python_version.description: Interpreter version inside the image, for kernel matching; empty = unknown.

ray_version.description: Ray version inside the image (ray engine).

ref.description: Image reference the pods run: `registry/repo:tag` or `registry/repo@sha256:…`.

ImageHistoryEntry.description: One `history` row of the image config — the instruction that produced a layer (BuildKit/docker record the Dockerfile line in `created_by`), joined to the layer it produced when it produced one. This is the closest an image gets to its Dockerfile.

empty_layer.description: True for instructions that changed only metadata (ENV, LABEL, CMD, …).

layer_digest.description: Digest of the layer this step produced; `null` for an empty layer.

size_bytes.description: Compressed size of that layer; `null` for an empty layer.

ImageInspect.description: What a catalog image looks like without pulling it (#10): the manifest and config blob read from its registry — platform, size, the container config (env, entrypoint, user, labels), the per-layer build history and the layers. One shape, shared with any other console that renders it.

digest.description: Digest of the manifest that was inspected (the platform manifest when `reference` resolved to an index).

platforms.description: Every platform the reference offers (one for a single-platform manifest).

reference.description: The reference that was inspected, as the catalog entry names it.

size_bytes.description: Sum of the inspected manifest's compressed layer sizes.

source.description: Which producer filled the document: `registry` (Bifrost read the manifest and config itself).

JobView.description: A job in the persistent, cross-cluster history (Phase 3, spec §5.5).

duration_secs.description: Wall-clock seconds once terminal; null while running.

status.description: Ray job status (PENDING | RUNNING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | STOPPED).

LocalRole.description:
A local user's role (ADR-0011: roles are a column on the user, resolved
per request — no claim staleness). Stored as TEXT in `local_users.role`;
the vocabulary mirrors the auth subsystem's Role type (kept as a separate enum so
core never depends on the auth package).

LocalUserView.description:
The public projection of a local user — everything EXCEPT the password
hash and the lockout internals that are nobody else's business.

LoginIdentity.description: The identity half of a login response.

LoginResponse.description:
`POST /api/v1/auth/login` success body. `token` is an opaque
`bfr_…` bearer credential (ADR-0011: stored, never signed).

expires_at.description: Unix seconds after which the token no longer authenticates.

NodeView.description:
A single Ray node (head or one worker) as Kubernetes sees it: the pod
KubeRay created for it, its scheduling/readiness, and the compute it
requests. Fields are `Option` because a pod may not yet be scheduled
(no IP/host) and a quantity may be unparseable or unset.

cpu.description:
CPU cores requested, summed across the pod's containers and parsed
from the K8s quantity (`500m` → 0.5). `None` when unset/unparseable.

gpu.description:
GPUs requested (`nvidia.com/gpu`), summed across containers. `None`
when the pod requests no GPU.

group.description: Worker-group name (`ray.io/group`); `None` for the head node.

host.description:
Kubernetes node the pod landed on (`spec.nodeName`); `None` before
scheduling.

is_head.description: Whether this is the cluster's head node.

memory_bytes.description:
Memory bytes requested, summed across the pod's containers (`2Gi` →
2147483648). `None` when unset/unparseable.

node_ip.description: Pod IP once scheduled (`status.podIP`); `None` before scheduling.

ready.description:
Whether the pod's `Ready` condition is true. Distinct from `phase`: a
pod can be `Running` but not yet `Ready`.

PolicyView.description:
`GET /api/v1/settings/policy` response: the effective policy plus its
provenance.

admission.description: project (or `"*"`) → admission limits (#7). Empty when none are configured.

budgets.description:
project → time-windowed compute budget (#77). Empty when none are
configured.

editable.description: Always true in v1 — the policy is editable via PUT.

environments.description: The environment catalog (#52); empty when none are configured.

images.description: The image catalog (#7/#10); empty when none are configured.

prices.description: resource → $/unit-hour; `null` when no price sheet is configured.

profiles.description: The profile catalog (#7); empty when none are configured.

quotas.description: project → (resource → limit). Empty when no quotas are configured.

source.description:
"file" (the untouched `--policy` boot seed) | "store" (edited via
PUT) | "none" (no policy configured at all).

storage.description: The storage catalog (#12); empty when none are configured.

workload_identity.description: project (or `"*"`) → workload identity (#20). Empty when none are configured.

PoolPurpose.description: What a pool's capacity is for (#4). `compute` (the default when absent) admits interactive clusters and jobs; `serving` admits only RayService-backed services, so long-lived serving replicas never compete with notebooks for the same queue.

PoolSpec.description: A shared capacity pool: flavors + a cohort to borrow from (ADR-0010).

cohort.description:
Name of the Kueue cohort this pool's ClusterQueue joins for elastic
borrowing.

elastic.description:
Whether workloads in this pool may be elastically resized (Kueue
elastic jobs / Workload Slices).

oneOf.description:
GPU sharing mode for this pool (#58). `None` inherits the platform
default (`[gpu] default_sharing` in the policy file, itself
defaulting to `whole-gpu`). A pool shared by more than one project
may not resolve to `time-slice` — enforced at admission by
the policy package's GPU admission logic, not here (core validates shape; tenancy is
known only at the API edge, where allocations live).

purpose.description: What the pool's capacity is for (#4); absent = `compute`.

PoolUsageView.description:
Live point-in-time usage of one pool (Slice 4): built from the pool's
latest stored ClusterQueue/LocalQueue observation plus the spec's
nominal quotas. NOT a timeseries — for history use `GET /api/v1/usage`.
`projects` is the per-LocalQueue (per-project) attribution; empty when
the observation predates per-LQ status or none exists.

sampled_at.description:
When the observation was recorded (unix seconds); `null` until the
pool reconcile loop has observed this pool.

PoolView.description:
A pool as the control plane serves it: the stored spec metadata plus
`total_nominal`, the per-resource sum of all flavors' nominal quotas.

generation.description: Bumps when the spec changes (same convention as clusters).

oneOf.description:
The pool's GPU sharing mode (#58); `null` = the platform default
(`[gpu] default_sharing`, itself defaulting to `whole-gpu`).

purpose.description: What the pool's capacity is for (#4); absent = `compute`.

total_nominal.description:
Resource key → summed nominal quota across flavors, as a string.
A resource key whose quantity fails to parse on ANY flavor is
omitted entirely (a partial sum would misreport capacity); the
failure is logged. Display math only — the spec stays authoritative.

ProfileSpec.description: A named cluster shape in the profile catalog (#7): the head/worker shape and image a cluster or job gets when its spec names this profile. Expansion fills zero-valued shape fields and refuses conflicting non-empty ones (400).

idle_timeout_secs.description: Default inactivity reap window applied to clusters using this profile; `null` = none.

max_workers.description: Cap on total worker replicas for clusters using this profile; `null` = unlimited.

name.description: Catalog name a spec refers to (`ClusterSpec.profile`, `RayJobSpec.profile`).

projects.description: Projects that may use this profile; empty = every project.

storage.description: Storage catalog entries (#12) every cluster or job from this profile mounts, in addition to any the request names itself. Resolved against the project at create time like a request's own `storage`.

ttl_seconds.description: Default absolute max-age cap applied to clusters using this profile; `null` = none.

ProjectGrant.description:
One project the caller holds a scoped grant in, and the roles held
there. A client that has to name a project — the JupyterLab extension
starting a cluster, say — reads this rather than guessing a default.

name.description: The project's name, as `ClusterSpec.project` takes it.

roles.description:
Snake_case role names held *in this project*: "viewer", "developer",
"operator", "admin". A caller needs "operator" (or "admin") to create
or stop a cluster there.

ProvidersResponse.description:
Which auth providers this deployment offers (login-page metadata; not
sensitive — the endpoint is public by design).

oneOf.description: OIDC configuration, when a validator is configured.

PutAllocation.description:
Request body for putting an allocation: `AllocationSpec` minus
`pool`/`project`, which come from the path. If the body still carries
them, they must match the path or the request is rejected.

RayJobSpec.description: Declarative spec for an ephemeral Ray job (#5): Bifrost provisions a dedicated RayCluster, runs `entrypoint` on it and tears the cluster down when the job finishes. Mirrors a KubeRay RayJob CR so the provisioner stays a thin translation.

entrypoint.description: The shell command Ray runs as the job (e.g. `python train.py`).

environment.description: Environment catalog name (#52) whose image, packages and env vars this job runs with; `null` = none. Accepted and stored; resolution arrives with the catalog issue.

head_cpu.description: Head CPU request; default "1" when empty.

head_memory.description: Head memory request; default "2Gi" when empty.

image.description: Container image for the head, the workers and the submitter.

profile.description: Profile catalog name (#7) whose shape fills zero-valued fields here; `null` = none.

ray_version.description: Ray version in `image`; defaults from the image tag when empty.

runtime_env_yaml.description: Ray runtime_env for the job as a YAML document, passed through verbatim; empty = none.

storage.description: Storage catalog entries (#12) delivered to the job's pods.

ttl_seconds_after_finished.description: Seconds the finished job's cluster is kept before KubeRay deletes it; default 60 when omitted.

RayJobSummary.description:
A Ray job normalized to a stable Bifrost shape (api-v1.md §5.6). Every
field is optional: Ray's own records vary by version and by whether the
job has started/finished. `status` is Ray's vocabulary verbatim
(`PENDING | RUNNING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | STOPPED`) — not snake_cased,
per §5.7. `start_time`/`end_time` are Ray's unix-millis timestamps.

end_time.description: Ray's `end_time` (unix millis); `None` while the job runs.

start_time.description: Ray's `start_time` (unix millis); `None` before the job starts.

RayJobView.description: An ephemeral Ray job as the control plane sees it (#5): the submitted intent plus the last observed KubeRay RayJob status.

cluster.description: Name of the RayCluster backing the job while it exists; `null` before provisioning and after teardown.

deployment_status.description: KubeRay deployment status (Initializing | Running | Complete | Failed | Suspended | ...).

finished_at.description: Unix seconds the job reached a terminal status; `null` while running.

gateway_url.description: Gateway address of the job's Ray dashboard/Jobs API while the cluster is registered; `null` otherwise.

message.description: Last status message from KubeRay/Ray, when any.

owner.description: Identity that submitted the job (server-stamped); `null` when unattributed.

queue.description: Kueue LocalQueue the job's cluster was admitted through; `null` when Kueue is not in use.

started_at.description: Unix seconds the Ray job started running; `null` until then.

status.description: Ray job status (PENDING | RUNNING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | STOPPED); empty until Ray reports one.

RegistryEntryView.description:
A gateway routing entry as the control plane may show it: where a
cluster is exposed and where its dashboard head lives, but never the
token itself (ADR-0003, security issue #4).

source.description: `static` = from the boot-time registry file; `dynamic` = registered by the reconciler for a managed cluster, job or service.

target.description: What the entry proxies to: `jobs` = a Ray dashboard/Jobs API; `serve` = a Ray Serve endpoint.

token_set.description: Whether the gateway holds a static Ray token for this cluster.

oneOf.description:
Reserved for per-entry validation/reachability checks. Always null
today: registry validation is fail-fast at startup, so every served
entry is valid by construction.

RegistryValidation.description: Placeholder shape for future per-entry health/validation results.

ResourceStat.description:
A single resource's capacity, and its used amount when known. `used`/
`total` are in the resource's natural unit: CPU in cores, GPU in device
count, memory in bytes. `used` is `None` when the cluster does not report
live utilization (e.g. a non-autoscaling cluster whose Ray dashboard has
no load-metrics report) — the tile then shows capacity only.

ResourceUtilization.description:
One resource's live utilization within a pool: `allocated` is the Kueue
reservation-ledger total (summed across flavors from the latest
ClusterQueue observation), `nominal` the summed flavor quotas from the
spec, `pct` = allocated / nominal × 100 (0 when nominal is 0 — a
percentage of nothing is undefined, and 0 keeps the type non-optional).

RoleMappingsView.description:
Group→role mappings from the OIDC auth config; shape mirrors
the auth subsystem's role-mapping type (a wire twin so the auth package stays free of
serialization/api deps).

RolesResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/access/roles` response. `mappings` is null when no OIDC
validator is configured (local-auth or dev mode): group→role mappings
are meaningless there — local users carry their role as a column.

editable.description: Always false in v1 — editing stays in the config file + restart.

source.description:
"file" (mappings from the OIDC auth config) or "local" (no OIDC
validator; roles live on the local user rows).

ServiceSpec.description: Declarative spec for a managed Serve service.

serve_config_v2.description:
The Serve application config (KubeRay `serveConfigV2`), passed
through verbatim as a YAML string — Bifrost does not interpret it.

storage.description: Storage catalog entries (#12) delivered to the service's pods.

worker_replicas.description:
Fixed worker replicas backing the service (autoscaling of Serve
deployments is Ray Serve's own concern).

gateway_url.description: Gateway address of the Serve endpoint while the service is registered; `null` otherwise.

owner.description: Identity that deployed the service (server-stamped); `null` when unattributed.

queue.description: Kueue LocalQueue the service's cluster was admitted through; `null` when Kueue is not in use.

state.description: Observed lifecycle state: provisioning | running | updating | ...

url.description: External Serve endpoint base URL, when ready.

StorageEntry.description: A catalog entry for private storage (#12): a Secret or PersistentVolumeClaim Bifrost delivers to the pods of any cluster, job or service that names this entry in its `storage` list. The API only ever sees names and paths; a Secret's contents never cross it.

claim_name.description: Name of the PersistentVolumeClaim in the workload namespace (`persistent_volume_claim` source only). Claims are namespace-local: the claim must live where the pods run.

mode.description: How the source reaches the pods: `env` injects every Secret key as an environment variable (secret source only); `file` mounts the source at `mount_path` — read-only for a Secret (credentials), read-write for a PersistentVolumeClaim (a data volume).

mount_path.description: Mount point inside the pods (`file` mode only); `null` for `env` mode.

name.description: Catalog name a spec refers to.

projects.description: Projects that may reference this entry; empty = every project.

secret_name.description: Name of the Kubernetes Secret in the workload namespace (`secret` source only).

source.description: What backs the entry: a Kubernetes Secret or a PersistentVolumeClaim. Absent = `secret`. A volume source is `file` mode only.

id.description: Stable job id (RFC 1123 label); the server generates `job-<8 hex>` when `null`.

UpdatePolicy.description:
Request body for `PUT /api/v1/settings/policy`. Section-replace
semantics: a present key replaces that whole section (`prices: null`
clears the price sheet; `quotas: {}` clears all quotas); an absent key
leaves that section untouched.

admission.description: Present replaces the whole admission map (`{}` clears it) (#7).

budgets.description: Present replaces the whole budget map (`{}` clears all budgets) (#77).

environments.description: Present replaces the whole environment catalog (`[]` clears it) (#52).

images.description: Present replaces the whole image catalog (`[]` clears it) (#7/#10).

prices.description: Present (incl. explicit `null`) replaces/clears the price sheet.

profiles.description: Present replaces the whole profile catalog (`[]` clears it) (#7).

quotas.description: Present replaces the whole quota map (`{}` clears all quotas).

storage.description: Present replaces the whole storage catalog (`[]` clears it) (#12).

workload_identity.description: Present replaces the whole workload_identity map (`{}` clears it) (#20). Never retroactive: workloads already admitted keep the ServiceAccount they were admitted with.

password.description: New password (min 8 chars); replaces the bcrypt hash.

UpgradeStrategy.description: How to roll out a new version of a service.

UsageGroup.description: One (project, pool, owner) group of the usage report.

cost_usd.description: Total cost in USD; `null` when no price sheet is configured.

owner.description: Identity the consumption is attributed to (#14); empty string = unattributed.

pool.description: Empty string = the project has no allocation.

project.description: Empty string = the pool-level aggregate row (Kueue path only).

budgets.description:
Time-windowed budget status per configured project (#77). Empty when
no `[budgets]` are configured. When the report is filtered to one
`project`, only that project's budget appears.

WorkerGroup.description:
A homogeneous group of Ray worker nodes.

Autoscaling in v0 is actuated exclusively through these replica bounds,
which translate to KubeRay worker-group fields — never by reading demand
from GCS (ADR-0002).

WorkerGroupNodes.description: One worker group and its nodes (api-v1.md §5.3).

desired.description:
Desired replicas: the group's `replicas` field, or `minReplicas` when
autoscaling leaves `replicas` unmanaged (ADR-0007). Per-group desired
counts are not in the RayCluster status, so this is the spec's answer.

name.description: The worker-group name (`groupName` in the RayCluster spec).

ready.description: Ready replicas: pods in this group that are `Running` and `Ready`.

WorkloadIdentityRule.description: Per-project workload identity (#20): the Kubernetes ServiceAccount the pods of a project's clusters, jobs and services run under. Keyed by project (or `"*"` for every project) in `PolicyView.workload_identity`. This is the seam a cloud IAM binding attaches to (EKS Pod Identity / IRSA, GKE Workload Identity): the platform binds a role to the ServiceAccount, Bifrost only names it on every pod template it renders, and the pods obtain credentials from the node's identity agent — no static credentials. Every field optional; a kind-specific field wins for its kind, an empty one falls back to `service_account`, and an empty `service_account` keeps the namespace default. The ServiceAccount must already exist in the workload namespace; the apply fails with a readable condition when it does not. Resolved at admission and pinned on the spec, so a later edit never reaches a running workload.

service_account.description: Default ServiceAccount for every workload kind (RFC 1123 subdomain, an existing ServiceAccount in the workload namespace); empty = the namespace default.

job_service_account.description: Overrides `service_account` for ephemeral RayJobs (requirement 5): the job's cluster pods and its submitter pod.

info.description: FOSS control plane for Ray clusters. All endpoints take a Bearer JWT (OIDC). Note: the Ray Jobs API is NOT documented here — it is served by hostname, each registered cluster's hostname proxying Ray's own /api/jobs/ surface through the federating gateway. This spec covers Bifrost's own control-plane routes.
info.title: Bifrost

tags.description: Cluster lifecycle. Reads need any authenticated role; create/terminate need Write on the cluster target (Operator or Admin). Mounted only when the lifecycle controller is enabled (`serve --kuberay-namespace`).
tags.name: clusters

tags.description: Ray Serve services (RayService). Deploy/update/delete need Write on the service target (Developer or Admin — deploying is code); reads are open to any authenticated role. KubeRay handles zero-downtime canary rollout.
tags.name: services

tags.description: Capacity pools and per-project allocations (ADR-0010): platform configuration, not app lifecycle. Reads need any authenticated role; create/delete/allocation mutations are Admin-only. Mounted only when a store is configured.
tags.name: pools

tags.description: Usage metering (Slice 4): resource-hours reports and the Prometheus gauge over the metered samples. Reads need Read on the cluster target (Viewer+) — consumption reporting is cluster data, not pool topology. Mounted only when a store is configured.
tags.name: usage

tags.description: Governance policy management (api-v1.md §5.16): the effective price sheet and per-project quotas. Admin-only. The `--policy` file is the boot-time default; the store row wins once edited via PUT, and every consumer (quota admission, cost estimates, usage roll-up) reads the store per request, so edits apply without a restart. Mounted only when a store is configured.
tags.name: settings

tags.description: The job gateway's routing table (ADR-0002). Admin-only: it is the credential-routing table. Static config today; dynamic registration of managed clusters is a follow-up.
tags.name: registry

tags.description: The persisted audit trail (api-v1.md §5.9): every authn/authz decision, mutation, and proxied gateway request, newest-first with seq-cursor pagination and CSV export. Rows are hash-chained for tamper-evidence (#59); `audit/verify` replays the chain. Reads need Read on the audit target — Admin or Auditor — and are themselves audited (`audit_read` rows). Mounted only when a store is configured.
tags.name: audit

tags.description: Local auth (ADR-0011): username/password login issuing opaque (unsigned) bearer tokens, personal access token management, provider metadata, and Admin-only local user management. `login` and `providers` are public; token routes are owner-scoped; user routes are Admin-only. Mounted only with `serve --local-auth` (except `providers`).
tags.name: auth

tags.description: Identity & access (api-v1.md §5.8): `identity` is 'who am I' for any authenticated caller (the dev identity when auth is disabled); `access/roles` is the Admin-only read of the effective role mappings. Mounted unconditionally.
tags.name: access

tags.description: Ephemeral Ray jobs (#5) and the persistent cross-cluster job history. Submit/stop need Write on the job target in the job's project (Developer or Admin); reads are open to any authenticated role, narrowed to the caller's projects.
tags.name: jobs

tags.description: The profile catalog (#7): named cluster shapes an administrator maintains in the policy (`PUT /settings/policy`), listed here filtered to the caller's projects. Reads need Read on the cluster target.
tags.name: profiles

tags.description: Governed environment catalog (#52): named base-image + pinned-package sets specs reference by name. Reads mirror the profile catalog's; the catalog itself rides the policy document.
tags.name: environments

tags.description: The image catalog (#7/#10): approved image references an administrator maintains in the policy (`PUT /settings/policy` `images`), listed filtered to the caller's projects, and inspected — manifest, config, layer history — straight from the registry without pulling. Reads need Read on the cluster target.
tags.name: images
